material_premises.fact: Terminal-Bench 4.0 frozen population is 66 tasks x 5 trials = 330 slots; 220 successes required; 12 tasks are hardware-incompatible, 18 hardware-compatible tasks are irreversibly zero (spent or contaminated), 0 completed; 36 creditable tasks remain, so the maximum attainable is 180 (54.5%) < 220 (66.4%).
The independently verified compiler computes upper = completed successes + remaining creditable tasks x trials; unrun slots of irreversibly zero tasks are forced to zero.

Best case for a carrier-only change: if k of the 12 hardware-incompatible tasks became compatible AND creditable (assumes none is contaminated), the bar becomes reachable only at k>=8, where it requires a perfect 220/220; at k=12 it requires 91.7% trial success.

Even with all 12 hardware-incompatible tasks added, a realistic requirement needs revival of irreversibly zero tasks: reviving 12 of the 18 gives 60 creditable tasks and a 73.3% trial pass-rate requirement; all 18 gives 66 tasks and 66.7%. Revival requires lifting the NO_REPLAY / contamination rule.

Anthropic reports Claude Opus 5.5 at 66.4% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (xhigh effort, standard error +/-2.6 points). A system with that rate, run only on the 36 creditable tasks, is expected to reach about 119.5 of 330 slots (36.2%) against 220 required; the frozen predicate is therefore not satisfiable by its own reference system.

evidence.excerpt: Terminal-Bench 4.0 results are reported for Claude Opus 5.5 at xhigh effort ... The standard error is +/-2.6 pts for Claude Opus 5.5.
evidence.assumption: Opus's rate on the 36-task subset equals its overall rate.

material_premises.fact: Even on the full 330-slot population, an exact clone of Opus 5.5 (true rate 66.4%) reaches >=220 successes with probability about 0.485 under an independent-trials binomial model; a point-estimate bar with no margin is close to a coin flip for the reference itself.

evidence.caveat: Independence across trials assumed; task clustering changes the variance but not the ~50% centre.

material_premises.fact: The Terminal-Bench 4.0 population is closed at 66 tasks (12 hardware-incompatible + 18 irreversibly zero + 36 creditable). The creditable set therefore cannot be enlarged by drawing new tasks; only the 12 hardware-incompatible tasks (if clean and runnable on an admissible carrier) or lifting NO_REPLAY for the 18 can enlarge it.

evidence.excerpt: Terminal-Bench 4.0 measures complete model-and-agent systems across 66 containerized professional computer tasks

conclusion: No admissible route, carrier, protocol-equivalence or creditability change INSIDE the frozen rules raises the verified upper bound to a realistic level. Carrier changes alone reach 220 only at 44 creditable tasks and then demand a perfect score; only lifting NO_REPLAY could make the requirement realistic. Independently of capability, the frozen predicate fails its own reference system (Opus 5.5 expected ~36% of slots under this accounting), so it cannot measure 'equal or better than Opus 5.5' and cannot be closed by capability work.
